description.narrative: Describe the main project goal; do not list outcomes and outputs (max 500 words)Sudan: Pathways to Peace aims to contribute to the country’s return to a peaceful future through a bottom-up conflict transformation strategy complementary to other existing tracks towards peace. In-depth analysis of conflict dynamics including conflict causes will allow for programmatic interventions that directly address and mitigate conflict drivers (historical and current), reducing violence and preventing conflict from escalating. Inclusive, community-owned dialogue processes of decision-making, prioritization, and ownership over solutions to conflict causes will contribute to peaceful co-existence within communities facing social cleavages and increasing tribal and ethnic polarization. Equally, systematic support to community-owned peace initiatives translating into localized ceasefire agreements brokered by civilian actors will contribute to sustaining and gradually expanding peace pockets through a bottom-up approach, while being fully cognisant and complementary of other peace tracks. Local agreements on power- and resource-sharing, on parameters for peaceful co-existence and the cessation of hostilities need to inform high-level mediation efforts of both ceasefire and political tracks, while track-1 decisions equally require translation into local conflict dynamics. The project will proactively build these bridges between Sudan’s communal peace infrastructure and the agenda-setting for, and participation in high-level fora outside the country aimed at determining the future of the Sudanese state. To this end, the project will focus on strategic locations in River Nile State (Atbara) and Central Darfur (Zalingei) with conditions conducive for the outlined work.
